404 Media recently reported a vulnerability in iCloud+'s "Hide My Email" feature that allows anyone to obtain a user's real email address. Apple is now saying the issue has been officially patched.

Apple says the security flaw in "Hide My Email" was patched earlier this month

If you're a subscriber to iCloud+ or Apple One, Apple's "Hide My Email" privacy feature can be a great tool for protecting your real email address.

Here's how Apple describes how it works on its official website:

However, according to a new report from 404 Media, "Hide My Email" has long had a flaw that could let anyone uncover the real email address linked to an Apple account. The disclosure has also prompted a new proposed lawsuit.

Apple said today that the vulnerability was officially patched earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that it "rolled out a fix on July 3, and the company said the issue is fully resolved."

This iCloud+ vulnerability was originally reported to Apple by Tyler Murphy in June 2025. After some initial communication, Apple claimed to have patched it, but Murphy later discovered the issue still existed. Hopefully it's truly fixed this time.

How often do you use the "Hide My Email" feature on iCloud+? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
